added_models_m210b_4_2_7.physical_plausibility: sigma 0.04 S/m (resistivity 25 ohm m) with eps_r 9 is a moist silty/clayey loam: GPR and geoelectrics references give clay and silt resistivities of roughly 1-100 ohm m (sigma 0.01-1 S/m) and loams 0.001-0.05 S/m; 4TU sites are Dutch clay/peat/sand polder soils where such losses occur. Loss tangent at 500 MHz sigma/(omega eps) = 0.16, so the medium is still low-loss enough for a 1.5 m target to give a weak but present apex. eps_r 9 is on the low side for a wet clay (often 15-30); keeping eps_r 9 keeps geometry and timing identical to the other models, and the attenuation set by sigma is the variable under test. Labelled as a plausible moist loam, not a wet clay
added_models_m210b_4_2_7.prediction_before_pilot: two-way soil loss 65.4 dB vs 49.1 dB at sigma 0.03 (+16.4 dB, low-loss formula); A0 about 0.219 x 10^(-16.4/20) = 0.033 (harness path). Joint clutter just below the mute is generated in the brick/sand layers and is nearly independent of the soil sigma, so max E_clutter stays about 1.76 and L (median) about 0.6-1.2 -> Lambda_est(0) about 18-36 (assumption)
